title: Asset
description:
A reusable piece of artwork placed on a `Map`.

Assets are the shared image layer behind `Token`, `Tile`, `AreaEffect` and `Aura` —
each of those points at one rather than carrying its own file, so the same door or token art
can be dropped onto a map many times at no extra cost.

An asset is more than a file path. Its `type` decides how the resource is interpreted — a
still image, a tiling pattern, a sprite sheet to animate, or an animated file — with the
details in `parameters`, and `components` can tint or animate it further.

Assets are library content in their own right: they belong to a module, campaign or system and
are browsable and taggable like any other entity.

- SeeAlso: `Token`, `Tile`, `AreaEffect`, `Component`

id.description:
The unique identifier for this asset.

A UUID string automatically generated when the asset is created. This serves as the
primary key in the Realm database.

name.description:
The display name of the asset.

## Examples
- `"Wooden Door"`

slug.description:
A URL-friendly identifier for the asset.

Used to link to the asset as `/asset/wooden-door`.

## Examples
- `"wooden-door"`

type.description:
How the resource is interpreted, as the raw value of an `AssetType`.

Use `typeValue` for the typed form.

## Examples
- `"image"`, `"pattern"`, `"spriteSheet"`, `"animatedImage"`

resource.description:
The file path of the artwork.

- Note: Resolved against the asset's container — its module, campaign or system directory.

## Examples
- `"assets/img/wooden-door.png"`

components.description:
Filters and animations baked into the asset.

Applied wherever the asset is used, unlike the components on an individual `Tile`.

- SeeAlso: `Component`

rank.description:
The manual sort position of the asset.

Lower values sort first.

tags.description:
Custom tags for categorization and filtering.

## Example Tags
- `"dungeon"`, `"furniture"`, `"token"`

parentId.description: The identifier of the group containing this asset in the library tree.
